sections.title: From livery stable *to landmark*

image.alt: The long brick barn with its new red roof, seen across a green field

body: The first barn here was built of wood around 1893. It burned to the ground in 1909 and was rebuilt in brick, then repaired after more fires in 1911 and 1915, leaving the building that stands today.

D.W. Gaston, Sr. acquired the property in 1909 and ran a full-service livery with his son, D.W. Gaston, Jr., until 1932. They rented and boarded horses and kept horse-drawn vehicles in repair for year-round Aiken residents and the Winter Colony.

Inside is the original carriage lift, still in working order, that moved carriages and equipment up to the second floor. It is the only operational lift of its kind in the country that the Friends know of.

sections.title: Rent *the barn*
sections.intro: The event room is 1,300 square feet, seating 80 at tables or 120 standing, and there is a conference room for meetings. Call to see the rooms; reservations are made in person at the barn, and requests with less than 30 days’ notice are up to the board.

sections.eyebrow: Friends of the Gaston Livery Stable
sections.title: Saved by *the community*
body: The Friends of the Gaston Livery Stable formed in 2011, a 501(c)(3) set up to buy, protect and restore the barn. They bought the property that December.

Since then volunteers have given more than 28,500 hours, including four groups of officers from the 442nd Signal Battalion leadership course at Fort Gordon, alongside gifts of money, goods and services from all over Aiken.

items.q: When can I tour the barn?
items.a: Guided tours run on the first and third Saturdays of each month from 10 am to 1 pm. For another day, call (803) 648-4123 to set up a tour.
The event room seats 80 at tables and chairs, or 120 standing.

items.q: Can we bring our own caterer?
items.a: Yes, and you’ll need one: the barn has no kitchen, so food is prepared before it arrives.
Join the Friends (mail the membership form to PO Box 5357, Aiken, SC 29804), donate, or buy a book or ornament at Howell Printing on Barnwell Avenue. Proceeds go toward the mortgage.
